about.title: Long Beach Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: A work injury in Long Beach rarely comes with a simple answer about who pays. Most of the time, workers' compensation covers the employee no matter who was at fault, and it is usually the only claim you can bring against your own employer. That is not always where things end, though. When someone outside your company played a part — a subcontractor on a job site, the owner of the property where you were working, the maker of a machine that failed, or another driver who struck you while you were making a delivery on Pacific Coast Highway or I-405 — a separate personal injury claim may exist alongside comp. Long Beach logged 2,135 injury collisions in 2025 within Los Angeles County's records, and some share of those involved people who were simply on the clock. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We connect you with an independent attorney who can review both paths, explain which ones apply to your situation, and handle the case on contingency.

whyChoose.title: Why Long Beach Workers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: We look past the comp claim
items.desc: Workers' compensation is generally the exclusive remedy against your employer, but a negligent third party — a subcontractor, property owner, equipment manufacturer, or another driver — can be held to account separately. The attorney you are matched with reviews whether that second avenue exists for you.

items.title: Deadlines are explained in plain terms
items.desc: California asks you to report an on-the-job injury to your employer within 30 days, and a third-party claim carries a two-year filing deadline. Knowing both dates early keeps your options open.

items.title: Protected from retaliation, and no fee unless you recover
items.desc: Retaliating against a worker for reporting an injury or filing a claim is illegal in California. The independent attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: If I'm already receiving workers' comp, can I still file a personal injury claim?
items.answer: Possibly. Comp is normally the only remedy against your employer, but it does not shield an outside party whose negligence contributed to your injury. If a subcontractor, property owner, equipment maker, or unrelated driver was involved, a separate claim may be available. An attorney can sort out how the two interact.

items.question: I was hit while driving a work van on Long Beach Boulevard. Who is responsible?
items.answer: Because you were on the clock, workers' compensation would typically cover your medical care and a portion of lost wages regardless of fault. If the other driver caused the crash, you may also have a third-party claim against that driver. Long Beach reported 2,135 injury collisions in 2025, with crashes tending to peak on Fridays between 5 and 7 p.m., so work-related traffic injuries are not unusual here.

items.question: What if my Long Beach employer pushes back after I report the injury?
items.answer: California law makes it illegal for an employer to retaliate against you for reporting an injury or pursuing benefits. Report the injury within 30 days and keep a copy of anything you submit. If you experience pushback, mention it to the attorney you are connected with so it can be addressed.
